copy:
This is the kind of love
I want us to grow into.
visual: COVER CONTRADICTION, earliest chronological beat, not a resolution. Frontal medium close view through the rain-speckled windshield of one charcoal right-hand-drive car already parked safely on the quieter curb at blue-hour. Exactly Aachu and Zuv sit in the front seats and point in opposite directions at the same instant: passenger Aachu extends only her right index finger toward the warm restaurant entrance visible across the divided road; driver Zuv extends only his left index finger toward the opposite direction indicated by the single centrally mounted route phone. Their eyes cut toward each other with matching mildly exasperated 'obviously this way' expressions—no anger, no smile, no culprit. The central phone shows only one simple blue route line bending back, one arrowhead and one dot, with no words or UI labels. Their opposite fingers, matching faces and shared car must read immediately as: two people, one evening, two confident directions. Preserve generous clean upper-middle paper for exact text while keeping faces, pointing hands and phone large enough for a thumbnail. The restaurant is the only building visible; the chai counter is not yet shown. No road traffic, reflections, extra hands, background people, duplicate phone, signage, happy ending, chai, scooter or motorbike.
emotion: comic disagreement inside an aspirational promise
pose: Both upper bodies remain seated and separately traceable inside the parked car. Aachu points across the road with her right hand while her left stays fully below crop. Zuv points the opposite way with his left hand while his right rests visibly on the steering wheel. Their eye-lines meet briefly. Preserve the natural two-inch height difference through shoulder and head scale.
wardrobe: Continuous same-evening outfit anchored to together-01.jpg: Aachu in a white wrap blouse, blue jeans, red shoes, and one red handbag on her own shoulder; Zuv in a pale-blue button shirt, charcoal trousers, and black-red shoes.
props: one charcoal right-hand-drive car, one centrally mounted route phone, one steering wheel, rain on windshield, distant unlabelled restaurant entrance

cta_intent: The loving cover line against an instantly readable opposite-directions disagreement opens the question: how do these two grow through ordinary friction?

copy:
I will still say,
“Don’t talk to me.”
visual: Medium side view outside the same safely parked car. Aachu has just closed her own passenger door and is taking one clear step toward the barrier. Without turning back, she raises her right palm once at shoulder height in an unmistakable quiet 'not now' gesture; her left hand owns the strap of her red handbag. Zuv has just stepped around the rear of the car but visibly stops in response: his forward foot freezes, his mouth closes mid-sentence, and his left hand lowers the single route phone with its screen now dark. His right hand stays relaxed beside his own body. The physical cause and reaction must read with no text: she asks for silence, he stops. No smile, no pursuit, no touch, no shouting, no background people, no vehicle movement.
emotion: a childish sentence carrying a real need
pose: Aachu moves away with one readable stop palm. Zuv's body shows interrupted forward motion, then restraint. Preserve clear hands, wrists, feet and car boundaries.
props: one closed car door, one dark lowered phone, one red handbag, one closed umbrella against the car
continuity_lock: The phone turns dark here. Slide 4 begins after Zuv pockets it and chooses not to follow.
cta_intent: The line feels familiar rather than cruel because the image shows a boundary, not an attack.

copy:
I hope we learn
which part to hear.
visual: Wide barrier-level side view that makes the empty distance the main subject while keeping the bodies readable. Aachu sits alone on the far-left end of the low stone barrier, facing the road and breathing. After stopping on slide 3, Zuv has visibly settled to wait: he now sits on the closed rear edge of the parked car at frame-right with ankles loosely crossed, both hands resting open on the car surface beside his own hips, phone fully hidden in his trouser pocket. Sitting down is the visible consequence that proves he is neither pursuing her nor preparing to leave. He looks toward the opposite side of the road rather than watching her, giving privacy while remaining in the same geography. Their red and black-red shoes point generally toward the shared centre gap. The closed umbrella and restaurant across the road anchor continuity. No chai counter emphasis, cups, vendor, gesture, touching or extra person.
pose: Aachu sits at one edge of the frame; Zuv is clearly seated on the closed rear edge of the car at the other, with both palms supported on the exterior car surface and no limb intersecting the car body. Body distance is widest here.
props: one parked car used as a waiting perch, phone fully pocketed, one closed umbrella, low stone barrier, distant restaurant glow
continuity_lock: Maximum body distance. Slide 5 changes from geography to Aachu's proof that she notices he stayed.
cta_intent: The viewer understands that mature love may look like doing less, not saying more.

copy:
Not “go away.”
Just:
“Give me a minute. Don’t go far.”

In the softly focused but readable mid-background, Zuv remains exactly where slide 4 left him beside the car, gaze politely turned away, both hands still pocketed, phone invisible. The closed deep-navy umbrella and the car rear-light make his position unmistakable. Aachu's expression changes from hard irritation to one small relieved exhale; no smile yet. Her body remains facing away, so the glance—not a pose—carries the beat. No chai, no touch, no reaching, no extra person or human reflection.
emotion: relief that the requested space did not become abandonment
pose: Aachu owns the foreground reaction; only Zuv's full but smaller waiting figure appears behind her. Her shoulder and his silhouette never overlap.
props: car rear-light and closed umbrella as location anchors; phone fully invisible
continuity_lock: She confirms that he stayed without crowding. Slide 6 begins when she chooses to close the distance herself.
cta_intent: This is the most sendable recognition line and the emotional centre of the deck.

copy:
And when I’m ready,

“Chai?”
visual: Low medium reaction two-shot beside the same parked car, with one clear diagonal sightline from Aachu's gesture to the chai counter. Aachu has visibly returned into Zuv's space from the barrier side; the gap is now half as large as slide 4. She does not touch him. With one small raised eyebrow and the first hint of a smile, she extends her right index finger directly toward the one nearby unlabelled roadside chai counter on the quiet-curb side. On its ledge sits one small metal kettle with one restrained plume of steam—the only chai clue—and exactly two empty dark-wood stools beneath it. Her left hand remains on her own handbag strap. Zuv follows her finger and looks at the steaming kettle; his shoulders loosen and a small relieved smile arrives. Both of his hands stay naturally in his own pockets; phone fully hidden. The restaurant remains glowing across the divided road, still awkward to reach. No chai has been poured, no glass, vendor, sign, biscuit, touch, extra person or second stall.
emotion: repair becoming light without a speech
pose: Aachu is the mover who returns and proposes the smaller date. Zuv receives the invitation with a restrained, relieved reaction. Keep natural two-inch height difference.
props: one parked car, one closed umbrella, one red handbag, one unlabelled chai counter, one steaming metal kettle, exactly two empty stools, distant restaurant
continuity_lock: Aachu initiates the repair. Slide 7 pays off the two stools and returns the original irritation as harmless comedy.
cta_intent: The heavy centre breaks into a spoken, everyday, desi invitation.

copy:
Not less irritated.
Just better
at coming back.
visual: Intimate low counter-level close two-shot at the one unlabelled roadside chai stall. Aachu and Zuv now occupy the exact two stools introduced empty on slide 6, angled toward each other. The plainly empty unbranded paper biscuit sleeve lies flat and untouched on the counter between them, visible but secondary. Exactly four hands, one action per hand, no fused fingers or grabbing. They are visibly still capable of irritating each other, but their bodies, gaze and stools have come back together. No vendor, third cup, extra biscuit, brand lettering, background person, romantic embrace or generic posed smile.
pose: Close comic action-reaction with exactly four traceable hands: Aachu left holds chai, Aachu right holds the last biscuit, Zuv left holds chai, Zuv right reaches with an open empty palm. The empty sleeve lies on the counter and is held by nobody.
wardrobe: Same continuous outfit, now slightly softened by the seated pose and warm stall light.
props: exactly two cutting-chai glasses, one last biscuit, one empty unbranded paper sleeve, two occupied dark-wood stools, parked car, closed umbrella, distant restaurant
